newsitem.title: GREECE: IONIAN BANK SUBSIDIARIES SEE PROFITS RISE 4.9PCT.
newsitem.headline: IONIAN BANK SUBSIDIARIES SEE PROFITS RISE 4.9PCT.

text.p: The subsidiaries of Greece's state Ionian Bank posted pretax profits of 3.575 billion drachmas in 1996 versus 3.408 billion in 1995, up 4.9 percent, the bank said in a statement.

Ionian Mutual Funds saw its pretax profit rise 3.54 percent to 1.1 billion drachmas in 1996, Ionian Leasing 11.36 percent to 1.0 billion, Ionian Finance 110.29 percent to 286 million and Ionian Securities 55.61 percent to 202.6 million drachmas, it said.

Ionian Hotels posted pretax profits of 576.6 million drachmas in 1996 from 554.3 million in 1995, an increase of 4.02 percent. Profits of Ionian Training increased 1.4 percent to 130 million drachmas, it added.
Subsidiary Ionian Investments had profits of 267.1 million drachmas, down 45.1 percent on 1995.
But Ionian's chairman Haris Stamatopoulos told a news conference earlier on Wednesday that the group's subsidiaries saw their profits rise by 7.3 percent.

"The subsidiaries of Ionian Bank had a more positive presence in 1996 showing a total increase in profits of 7.3 percent. This will have a positive effect on the bank's consolidated results," Stamatopoulos told a news conference.
Ionian Bank's profits before taxes and provisions fell 69.7 percent to about 5.0 billion drachmas and would not pay a dividend for fiscal 1996, said Stamatopoulos.

Consolidated pretax profits of Ionian Mutual Funds, Ionian Leasing, Ionian Invest, Ionian Finance and Ionian Securities rose 14.45 percent to 824.8 million drachmas in the first two months of 1997 compared to 720.7 million in the same period in 1996, it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
